row_account.what: row accounting only (primary points; every repeat and seed is a row): not an agreement figure

method.interval: 95% nominal percentile interval of a game-level bootstrap (whole games drawn with replacement); simulated coverage is about 89-94% at 10-17 games
method.estimator: sum of per-decision values / number of decisions (every decision weighs the same)
method.primary: judge: the one call per decision (repeat 0); step bots: mean over all predefined seeds

agreement.prefix: all primary points: the move list agrees with an accepted one up to the plan's own end (first chance event, attack or end of turn)
agreement.full_plan: full-scope points only, complete turns only: the same listed plan as an accepted move list AND what follows a chance event equal label by label; a judge plan that stops at a chance event, and a step-bot turn pg_pos cut at a draw card, are not comparable

method.sign_flip: exact test over games up to 16 games, seeded Monte Carlo (100000 draws) beyond; a direction needs p < 0.05 as well
method.failed_judge_rows: miss: a judge row without a valid choice (an invalid label, a reply cut at the cap, a blocked prompt, any finish but STOP) scores 0 in the prefix and in the full-scope numbers, never "not comparable"; the count is in report.failed_judge_rows
method.multiplicity: no adjustment for several contrasts (with the two default contrasts the chance of at least one false direction is about 5%)

contrasts.reason: the interval excludes 0 and the sign-flip test over games agrees
the interval excludes 0 and the sign-flip test over games agrees; computed on 86 of 90 decisions, 4 not comparable for both bots (dropped, not scored)

failed_judge_rows.what: such a row counts as a MISS (agreement 0) in the prefix and in the full-scope scoring, but only if it is otherwise a consistent row (settings, plan-list identity, prompt hash, a stop reason that agrees with the finish fields recorded beside it, a stored reply that really holds no valid choice: rows are not authenticated, this is what the row's own fields can show); the count and the rows are reported plainly (report.failed_judge_rows) and a WARNING is printed when more than 20% of the primary judge decisions failed. It can only lower the judge's rate and the prefix score; in the full-scope CONTRAST a miss pair is kept where an answered plan that stops at a chance event would have been dropped, so the contrast can move toward zero, and a game that exists only because of a miss does not count toward the min-games gate. A step-bot row without a plan, a missing row or any other problem still stops the compare

plan_list_label_check.what: positions where some plans' own labels do not name them (fit several plans or cannot be followed): a bot or recorded move list using such a label is AMBIGUOUS, and the judge is shown plans that look identical
